### Pray for Those Who Abuse You
Author: John Piper
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/pray-for-those-who-abuse-you
Passage: Luke 6:27-28
Points:
- Jesus commands believers to pray for all who oppose them, from difficult relatives to dangerous persecutors.
- Praying brings God directly into conflict, turning to Him rather than taking vengeance.
- Prayers for enemies should reflect the Lord's Prayer, asking for their repentance, forgiveness, and spiritual transformation.
- True Christian love is not complete if it seeks only an enemy's earthly welfare rather than their eternal joy in God.

### A Prayer for Your Enemies
Author: Emily Rose Massey
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-daily-prayer/praying-for-your-enemies.html
Passage: Luke 6:27-28
Points:
- Hurtful words and false accusations present an immediate choice between bitter offense and Christ-like forgiveness.
- Intentionally praying for those who mistreat you prevents resentment and bitterness from taking root.
- Harboring unforgiveness creates spiritual bondage, whereas asking God to bless an opponent frees the heart.
- Believers cannot love enemies in their own strength but must depend on the Holy Spirit to extend mercy.
